piece.title: String Quartet in C major, Hob.III:32, Op.20 No.2
piece.why: Cello leads in its tenor register above Violin II and viola while Violin I is silent, then Violin I takes over, then Violin II (doubled by viola) carries the line under a Violin I pedal.

roster.label: Quartet that lost its viola: 2 violins, cello, + a clarinet

plan.summary: The tune starts in the tenor (the original cello line). In this cover the clarinet plays it in its warm low register while the real cello takes over the viola's bass figures. From bar 8 the advanced violinist plays the high first-violin melody, and the second violin follows it in thirds. In the final bars the second violin takes the descending scale tune, with the clarinet playing the parallel line below, the cello playing the low G pedal and violin 1 holding the high G. Each player keeps one line nearly all the way through, and every part fits its player's range with no octave shifts.

assignments.reason: The opening tune is in the tenor (G3–G4). The clarinet's warm low register sings it clearly and handles the quick 16ths and triplets easily.
The viola's arpeggios and repeated C's are the real bass line here (C3 and up). It sits well on the cello and stays below everything else.
At the close the cello moves to its own low G2 pedal, the true bass for the ending.

Violin 2 keeps its own part throughout. It is the inner accompaniment at first, then plays thirds under the high tune in bars 8–11 and takes the descending scale melody in bars 12–14. All of it is in range (B3–D6).
The first-violin melody enters in bar 7 and climbs to D6 with busy 16ths in bars 8–11, so it goes to the advanced violinist. It then holds the closing G5 pedal.
In the final bars the viola plays a scale line in parallel just under the violin 2 tune (G3–E5). The clarinet is free by then and blends well with it.
